svg.title: Seizure safety, ambulance triggers and breathing check
svg.desc: Working Australian seizure first-aid card. If the person is unresponsive and not breathing normally, including gasping or uncertain breathing, call Triple Zero and start CPR on a firm surface. Otherwise stay, start timing, clear nearby hazards, move the person only from immediate danger, protect the head with a soft flat item and let movements happen without restraint. Do not put anything in the mouth or force a roll. Call Triple Zero as soon as any listed trigger applies, including more than five minutes, another seizure before recovery, a first or unknown seizure, an unknown person or no plan, water, known diabetes or possible pregnancy, injury, breathing trouble, delayed response, a different pattern, food, fluid or vomit in the mouth, or doubt. Do not wait for five minutes when another trigger already applies. After movements stop, use CPR for abnormal breathing, the recovery-position card for an unresponsive person breathing normally, or rest and observation when responsive. If Triple Zero will not connect, keep care going and use Chapter 3's life-threatening-emergency contact path; do not leave the person merely to seek signal. Prescribed rescue medicine is only for a trained carer following the current plan and exact product instructions. Give nothing by mouth until fully awake and alert.
svg.text: SEIZURE — KEEP SAFE, TIME, WATCH
WORKING CARD · USE ALL 3 PARTS
WARNING — CLINICAL AND HANDS-ON REVIEW NEEDED
Subjective estimates: source match 95%; new layout 60%.
These are not probabilities of safety, treatment success or survival.
Side-position timing during convulsions and remote escalation remain unresolved.
Use all parts together. Follow 000 and the person’s current plan.
UNRESPONSIVE AND NOT BREATHING NORMALLY?
Gasping or unsure counts. Call 000 and use a firm surface.
Start CPR now. Do not work through this card first.
WHILE MOVEMENTS ARE HAPPENING
Stay. Start a timer now.
Clear hard or sharp objects. Move only from immediate danger.
Protect the head with a soft, flat item such as folded clothing.
Let the movements happen. Watch breathing when safely able.
DO NOT
• do not hold the person down or restrain the movements
• do not force the mouth open or put anything in it
• do not force a roll; use the side-position branch below when safe
CALL 000 AS SOON AS ANY ONE APPLIES
Do not wait for every sign or for the seizure to stop.
• more than five minutes
• another seizure starts before
the person fully recovers
• first or unknown seizure
unknown person or no seizure plan
• happened in water
• known diabetes or may be pregnant
• injury or breathing trouble
• not responsive five minutes
after movements stop
• different from the plan or
the person’s usual pattern
• food, fluid or vomit in the mouth
• any doubt or concern
A five-minute threshold is one trigger — not a wait-before-help rule.
AFTER MOVEMENTS STOP: CHECK RESPONSE + BREATHING
UNRESPONSIVE + ABNORMAL, GASPING OR UNSURE BREATHING
Call 000. Firm surface. Start CPR. Use the CPR/AED cards.
UNRESPONSIVE + BREATHING NORMALLY
Use the recovery-position card. Keep watching breathing.
RESPONSIVE
Rest, reassure, check for injury and keep watching.
000 will not connect? Keep care going. Use Chapter 3’s
life-threatening-emergency contact path.
Do not leave the person merely to seek signal.
WITH A KIT
• use a timer and the current plan
• use soft, flat head padding
• rescue medicine: trained carer only
follow the plan + product instructions
WITHOUT A KIT
• use a phone or watch to time
• use folded clothing for the head
• same safety, call and breathing steps
• no improvised rescue medicine
Nothing by mouth until fully awake and alert.
There is no fixed “all clear” time.
WORKING DRAFT — follow 000 and the person’s current seizure plan
